book.title: El cocinero de su majestad: Memorias del tiempo de Felipe III
book.author: Manuel Fernández y González

unity.instructions: `chapters` is the outline of a novel, a summary of each of its chapters in order; `threads` lists the questions its story raises and where each is settled; `people` lists its characters and what changes for each. How much are the chapters parts of one whole?
criteria: The chapters are episodes that could come in another order, or be left out, without the rest changing
The chapters follow one another in time, and several lead to nothing later
Most chapters follow from what came before and prepare what comes after
Every chapter follows from what came before and prepares what comes after: the whole is one action

cause.instructions: `chapters` is the outline of a novel, a summary of each of its chapters in order; `threads` lists the questions its story raises and where each is settled; `people` lists its characters and what changes for each. Why do the main events of the story happen, mostly?

criteria.people: Because of what the characters decide and do
criteria.events: Because of earlier events of the story
criteria.chance: Because of outside events or coincidence
criteria.none: With no evident connection between them

settled.instructions: `chapters` is the outline of a novel, a summary of each of its chapters in order; `threads` lists the questions its story raises and where each is settled; `people` lists its characters and what changes for each. What becomes of the questions the story raises?
criteria: Most of what the story raises is dropped and never settled
Some of what the story raises is settled, and several things are dropped
Nearly all that the story raises is settled by the end, or pointedly left open

ending.instructions: `chapters` is the outline of a novel, a summary of each of its chapters in order; `threads` lists the questions its story raises and where each is settled; `people` lists its characters and what changes for each. What brings about the resolution at the end?

criteria.prepared: Another character's action, or an event, that the story had prepared
criteria.unprepared: An outside event or a stroke of luck that the story had not prepared

change.instructions: `chapters` is the outline of a novel, a summary of each of its chapters in order; `threads` lists the questions its story raises and where each is settled; `people` lists its characters and what changes for each. What has become of the central character by the end?

criteria.same: They are as they were at the start, and nothing new is revealed of them
criteria.seen: They are as they were at the start, but the reader sees them differently
criteria.steps: They have changed, by steps that the chapters show
criteria.abrupt: They have changed all at once, with no steps leading to it

rising.instructions: `chapters` is the outline of a novel, a summary of each of its chapters in order; `threads` lists the questions its story raises and where each is settled; `people` lists its characters and what changes for each. How does the pressure on the central characters move across the book?
criteria: The pressure on the central characters is much the same from beginning to end
The pressure on the central characters rises and falls with no direction
The pressure on the central characters rises, with rests, to a height near the end

wants.instructions: `chapters` is the outline of a novel, a summary of each of its chapters in order; `threads` lists the questions its story raises and where each is settled; `people` lists its characters and what changes for each. How many of its people want something of their own?
criteria: One character wants something, and the rest are there to help or to hinder
Two sides want opposite things, and everyone belongs to one of them
Several characters each want something of their own, and their wants get in each other's way

beyond.instructions: `chapters` is the outline of a novel, a summary of each of its chapters in order; `threads` lists the questions its story raises and where each is settled; `people` lists its characters and what changes for each. How far do its concerns go beyond the people in it?
criteria: The story concerns only the events and the people in it
The story touches in passing on something that matters beyond the people in it
Something that matters beyond the people in it is at the centre of the story

spare.instructions: `chapters` is the outline of a novel, a summary of each of its chapters in order; `threads` lists the questions its story raises and where each is settled; `people` lists its characters and what changes for each. Is there a storyline in it that could be taken out without the main story losing anything?

turn.instructions: `chapters` is the outline of a novel, a summary of each of its chapters in order; `threads` lists the questions its story raises and where each is settled; `people` lists its characters and what changes for each. Does the story take a turn that the chapters before it did not lead one to expect, and that still follows from them?
